newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks correct after testing 1,200 level.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks correct after testing 1,200 level.

text.p: Greek shares slipped 0.58 percent on Friday after testing the 1,200 level, peaking at 1,203 points during the session.
Analysts expected a further advance next week sparked by an improved January revised CPI figure which showed inflation slowing to at 6.8 percent.
"The index should trade around 1,180 to 1,200 points in the next two sessions," said analyst Takis Niarchos at Hellenic American Securities.
The September current account deficit, which fell provisionally to $8.0 million from $289.1 million in September 95 would also boost sentiment, he added.
The Athens general share index finished 0.58 percent or 6.92 points lower at 1187.80 points from Thursday's 1194.72, after opening at 1195.13.
Losers led gainers 109 to 105 with 34 issues unchanged on 248 traded. Turnover was 14.0 billion drachmas on volume of 5.6 million shares.
Banks lost 0.94 percent, construction shares dropped 0.99 percent along with industrials, down 0.66 percent. Small-caps ended 0.60 percent lower.
Insurance shares fell 0.36 percent and leasing lost 0.79 percent.
Only investment stocks ended up 0.39 percent.
